projects.functionalBrief: Plan a two-storey private home for a household seeking connected family living, quiet bedrooms, and direct access to a sheltered garden and pool terrace. Separate guest arrival from household service routes, provide secure storage and utility functions, and make the glazed living level comfortable and private after dark.
programme: Kitchen with pantry and utility access
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Place the entrance, stair, and a compact service core toward the arrival side; keep kitchen and utility close to service access while the living and dining rooms open to the garden. Locate bedrooms upstairs behind the timber screen, with the principal suite at the quieter end. Keep the pool terrace directly accessible from living spaces, provide a continuous step-free ground-floor route, and keep pool equipment and maintenance access outside the principal family circulation.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 390–450 m² gross internal area over two storeys, with four bedrooms, on a level 1,000–1,300 m² landscaped plot; pool and terraces are additional external area. All dimensions and areas are approximate and subject to survey and local planning requirements.
projects.structuralSystem: Use a reinforced-concrete frame with a regular column grid of roughly 4.5–6 m, concrete floor plates, and a reinforced-concrete stair/core. Support the upper projection with a designed transfer beam or cantilever slab, limiting its reach to a practical approximately 2.5–3.5 m pending engineer verification; use non-loadbearing rendered infill and independent timber screen supports.
projects.constructionLogic: Build foundations and the concrete frame after geotechnical confirmation, then install waterproofed roof and terrace falls before façade finishes. Detail the cantilever with engineered reinforcement and thermal breaks where needed; provide drained, ventilated fixings for limestone and timber, sill flashing at full-height glazing, movement joints, and concealed gutters with accessible outlets. Sequence pool construction and testing independently from the house waterproofing, with overflow routed to a planted soakaway or approved drainage point.
projects.environmentalResponse: Orient principal living glazing toward the garden with external roof overhangs and adjustable vertical timber screens to control low-angle sun and privacy. Use cross-ventilation where weather and security permit, with ceiling fans and efficient mechanical cooling as a back-up; provide operable shaded openings rather than relying on sealed glass. Capture roofwater for landscape use, use permeable garden paving, and select drought-tolerant trees and planting suited to the eventual site climate.

projects.functionalBrief: Provide a compact year-round mountain home for a family needing warm shared living, private sleeping rooms, and sheltered outdoor outlooks in a cold, wet, sloping setting. Organize storage, plant, and wet functions to buffer uphill exposure, with a vestibule for outdoor gear and straightforward access for maintenance and snow-season use.
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Step the two-level footprint along verified contours, placing entry, stair, bathrooms, laundry, and storage against the uphill edge and opening living areas toward the valley. Put sleeping rooms on the quieter upper level, with one accessible bedroom and bathroom on the entry level if required. Maintain a clear downhill escape route and an all-weather service approach, while keeping retaining walls, roof discharge, and emergency access clear of the main path.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 190–230 m² gross internal area over two levels, with three bedrooms plus a flexible study/guest room, on a steep wooded plot of approximately 900–1,400 m². Approximate figures only; final footprint, access, and retaining extent depend on topographic and geotechnical surveys.
projects.structuralSystem: Use reinforced-concrete strip/stepped foundations and a modest reinforced-concrete lower-level retaining structure designed for site-specific soil and seismic conditions. A braced timber frame or engineered timber floor/roof system above can carry the upper level and steep gable; use a simple 3.6–4.2 m planning bay, with engineered ridge/rafter members and steel hold-downs rather than unsupported long spans.
projects.constructionLogic: Complete survey, slope-stability assessment, and uphill diversion drainage before excavation; bench only the required building pads and construct retaining walls with free-draining backfill, filter fabric, and maintainable outlets. Build the stone base as a drained rainscreen or properly tied masonry veneer over the structural wall, then erect the timber frame and insulated roof. Use a ventilated underlay, securely fixed slate, snow guards above paths, flashed eaves and ridge, and a raised ventilated timber-to-stone junction; route roof and hillside runoff to stable, erosion-protected discharge points.
projects.environmentalResponse: Place controlled glazing toward useful winter sun and valley views while limiting openings on the cold uphill face; provide deep eaves and external shutters or screens for summer glare and storms. Specify continuous insulation, airtight construction, thermal-bridge control, and a compact vestibule, with balanced ventilation or controlled purge openings as appropriate. Use the steep roof for reliable rain and snow shedding, collect rainwater where climate and maintenance allow, and protect existing trees while restoring disturbed slopes with native ground cover and contour drainage.

projects.functionalBrief: Design a narrow-plot urban home for a small family that needs bright shared rooms, privacy from a close street, and flexible work or guest space without relying on a dark internal corridor. Keep daily services compact and accessible, and make vertical movement, deliveries, waste handling, and emergency escape legible on the constrained site.
programme: Planted open-to-sky lightwell and roof terrace
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Use a compact stair and wet-service spine along one party edge, with rooms opening across the central lightwell and short bridges/landings rather than long corridors. Place entry, living, kitchen, and a small guest WC at ground level; arrange bedrooms and study on upper floors with the principal bedroom away from street noise. Preserve a clear protected stair route to the street, coordinate any required secondary escape with local code, and maintain independent access to rainwater, drainage, and rooftop equipment for service.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 210–250 m² gross internal area across three storeys, on an urban plot approximately 6–7 m wide by 18–22 m deep (about 110–150 m²), with three bedrooms and one flexible room. Approximate dimensions and floor areas require confirmation against survey, setbacks, fire rules, and allowable floor-area ratio.
projects.structuralSystem: Use a reinforced-concrete stair/service spine and a regular reinforced-concrete beam-and-slab frame with short 3.5–4.5 m spans suited to the narrow plan. Maintain a continuous lateral system around the stair and party-wall lines, subject to structural and seismic design; use lightweight non-loadbearing partitions and supported terracotta screen panels with corrosion-resistant brackets.
projects.constructionLogic: Establish party-wall protection, utility diversions, and a confined-site construction and lifting plan before excavation; use a designed raft or combined/strip foundation based on neighboring structures and soil. Construct the frame and lightwell edges with falls and waterproof upstands, then install drained façade finishes and mechanically supported terracotta screens. Flash all lightwell openings, provide accessible rainwater downpipes and leaf guards, use a maintainable overflow route, and coordinate fire-rated openings, smoke ventilation, handrails, and non-slip stair finishes before fit-out.
projects.environmentalResponse: Use the planted lightwell as a daylight and stack-ventilation source, with appropriately sized operable openings and insect screens; provide mechanical extract in bathrooms and kitchen. Recess street-facing windows behind sliding terracotta screens for privacy and glare control, and shade the roof terrace. Collect roof runoff in a modest tank for irrigation or cleaning, direct lightwell overflow to approved drainage, and select compact shade-tolerant planting with root containment and safe maintenance access.

projects.functionalBrief: Create a two-storey family home in an arid setting that balances private rooms with shared living around two sheltered courts. The household needs shaded outdoor sitting, clear guest arrival, flexible work/guest accommodation, and low-maintenance finishes that tolerate heat and dust.
programme: Two planted courts and upper loggia
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Organize the living and dining rooms around the larger shaded court, with the second court bringing daylight to quieter bedroom and study areas. Place the kitchen beside a screened service yard and near the entry for deliveries; group bathrooms and stairs into a compact service zone. Separate guest and family circulation where practical, provide direct kitchen/service access, and maintain a clear stair and ground-floor route to the site access for egress and emergency response.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 330–390 m² gross internal area over two storeys, accommodating four bedrooms and one flexible room on an approximately 800–1,100 m² arid-plateau plot. Courtyards and upper loggia are external/semi-external areas; all dimensions are approximate and subject to site and planning review.
projects.structuralSystem: Use a reinforced-concrete frame and slab with a regular 4–5 m bay, reinforced-concrete stair/core, and non-loadbearing local sandstone facing or engineered loadbearing masonry only where confirmed by structural design. Keep the upper loggia and roof edges within ordinary beam/slab spans; use lintels or concealed beams over openings and provide movement joints in long stone-faced elevations.
projects.constructionLogic: Confirm local stone properties and foundation conditions, then build the frame, roof falls, and court drainage before installing stone cladding. Mechanically anchor stone veneer with corrosion-resistant ties, provide a drained cavity, through-wall flashing, weeps, and flexible movement joints; use compatible lime-based mortar where masonry is exposed. Waterproof court paving and planters with root-resistant membranes, positive falls, overflow drains, and accessible cleanouts; sequence screens and recessed frames after façade drainage layers are tested.
projects.environmentalResponse: Keep larger openings to shaded courts and cooler orientations, with deep reveals and external timber screens to limit direct solar gain; use smaller protected openings on hot exposures. Provide cross-ventilation between court-facing rooms where privacy allows, ceiling fans, and high-level purge ventilation while maintaining secure night ventilation. Use the courts for drought-tolerant shade planting, permeable surfaces, and modest captured roofwater; avoid permanent high-volume water features and provide overflow to a designed site drainage route.

projects.functionalBrief: Plan a single-storey coastal home for a family needing an accessible daily living level, protected outdoor circulation, and robust storage during intense monsoon weather. Keep wet rooms, laundry, and equipment easy to maintain, and provide secure shutters and sheltered arrival without sacrificing cross-breezes in milder conditions.
programme: Rain garden, cistern, and service court
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Set the elongated footprint along verified contours, with the raised plinth and verandah on the downhill garden side and entry near the uphill service approach. Place living and dining centrally, bedrooms at quieter ends, and kitchen, bathrooms, laundry, and plant functions along an efficient service band. Ensure the verandah is not the sole required escape route, provide compliant external egress from sleeping areas as required, and keep roofwater channels and maintenance paths separate from accessible entrances.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 200–240 m² gross internal area on one level, with three bedrooms, on a sloping coastal plot of approximately 1,000–1,600 m². Verandah and service-yard area are additional; approximate levels and plinth height require flood, topographic, and local code checks.
projects.structuralSystem: Use a reinforced-concrete or engineered masonry plinth founded to geotechnical recommendations, supporting a lightweight timber roof structure with engineered rafters/trusses at roughly 3.5–4.5 m spacing. Laterite masonry may be structural only where strength and detailing are verified; otherwise use it as tied infill or a rainscreen. Provide roof bracing, uplift anchors, and corrosion-resistant connections designed for local wind and seismic conditions.
projects.constructionLogic: Survey flood levels, slope runoff, and soil bearing before setting the finished floor and plinth; phase earthworks to avoid destabilizing the slope. Construct the plinth with a damp-proof course, capillary break, and accessible inspection line, then erect the timber roof and install underlay, battens, securely clipped clay tiles, ventilated ridge, and generous flashed eaves. Size gutters for intense rainfall, include leaf access and overflow, route rain chains into stone channels and a cistern/soakaway, and detail shutters, verandah thresholds, and roof-to-wall junctions against wind-driven rain.
projects.environmentalResponse: Orient paired openings across the plan for cross-ventilation but protect them with operable timber shutters and the deep verandah during wind-driven rain. Use the steep tiled roof and ventilated ridge to exhaust hot air, with ceiling fans and insect screens; include high-level openings where safely operable. Harvest roofwater in a screened, maintainable cistern, provide overflow to planted channels sized for storm events, and use salt- and humidity-appropriate fixings with native coastal planting that stabilizes disturbed soil.

projects.functionalBrief: Develop a mid-rise multi-family housing proposal that provides practical, daylit apartments and shared outdoor space while maintaining a porous neighborhood-scale ground plane. Residents need secure entries, accessible routes, clear waste and servicing operations, and shaded communal areas that can be managed without compromising privacy or fire access.
programme: Approximately 36–48 apartments in varied one-, two-, and three-bedroom layouts
Three residential wings and shared planted court
Accessible ground-floor entries and circulation galleries
Rain gardens, paths, and shaded terraces
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Arrange three mid-rise wings as an open-sided U around a shared court, with apartment entrances from daylit galleries and lifts/stairs grouped in code-compliant cores. Put the community room at ground level facing the garden, while keeping waste, electrical, pump, and delivery functions near a screened service edge. Provide accessible continuous routes from street and accessible parking to units and communal facilities; maintain fire-appliance access, separated protected escape stairs, and unobstructed discharge routes in accordance with local regulations.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 4–5 storeys and 4,500–6,000 m² gross floor area, about 36–48 homes, on an approximately 2,800–3,800 m² urban site. Unit mix, parking, height, open-space ratio, and capacity are indicative only and must be reconciled with local planning, accessibility, and fire requirements.
projects.structuralSystem: Use a reinforced-concrete frame with typical apartment bays of approximately 5.5–7 m, flat slabs or beams/slabs, and reinforced-concrete lift/stair cores for lateral stability. Coordinate column positions with parking and apartment planning; use nonstructural brick infill or framed façade assemblies, with the linking canopy carried on independent steel or concrete supports rather than relying on long unsupported apartment-wing spans.
projects.constructionLogic: Build foundations and cores after geotechnical, utility, and fire-access coordination; repeat floor plates to simplify formwork and services distribution. Detail brick as drained cavity or properly tied veneer with movement joints and lintels, and anchor perforated aluminum screens to replaceable subframes. Waterproof balconies and roof edges with falls, upstands, drip edges, and accessible outlets; construct the canopy with engineered drainage and expansion joints. Grade the court to planted rain gardens with overflow connections, and phase landscape works after heavy deliveries to protect permeable surfaces.
projects.environmentalResponse: Orient apartment rooms for useful daylight and cross-ventilation where exposure, noise, and security permit; use recessed balconies and perforated screens to shade glazing without blocking ventilation. Provide efficient lifts, ceiling fans, high-performance glazing appropriate to climate, and roof solar/plant zones coordinated with the canopy. Use native shade trees, permeable basalt paths, and rain gardens with safe overflow, plus roofwater storage for landscape irrigation; ensure the court remains accessible and receives enough daylight for planting.

projects.functionalBrief: Provide a compact family residence that turns inward for privacy and comfort in a hot, dry climate, while bringing daylight and air to shared rooms through one planted courtyard. Residents need legible separation between social and private areas, shaded verandas, and a small, maintainable water element that does not create excessive consumption or safety risk.
programme: Planted courtyard, veranda, and shallow stepped water court
projects.floorOrSiteOrganization: Arrange rooms around a square open-to-sky court, with living and dining rooms opening to the veranda and kitchen near a screened service approach. Place bedrooms upstairs or in the quieter wing, with bathrooms and stair grouped for efficient plumbing and circulation. Treat the shallow water steps as a guarded, nonessential courtyard feature with a bypass route; keep the primary accessible route level and unobstructed, and provide direct street access and compliant protected stair egress.
projects.areaOrScale: Proposal-stage allowance: approximately 280–330 m² gross internal area over two storeys, with three bedrooms and one central courtyard, on an approximately 600–850 m² dry-region plot. The water court is shallow and limited in extent; final dimensions, levels, and room count are approximate and subject to local approvals.
projects.structuralSystem: Use a reinforced-concrete frame and stair core with approximately 4–5 m bays, concrete slabs, and nonstructural handmade brick infill and perforated fired-clay jaali panels. Provide independent lintels or reinforced-concrete beams over court-facing openings, with lateral stability from the core and selected shear walls; secure jaali panels to engineered secondary frames with allowance for thermal movement.
projects.constructionLogic: Set out the court, structure, and service risers together to prevent conflicts; provide concrete foundations and slab edges designed for local soil and seismic conditions. Install cavity drainage, damp-proofing, and compatible lime mortar at brickwork, with flashing and drip edges at jaali and veranda transitions. Waterproof the court basin separately from adjacent rooms, use non-slip stone treads and safe edges, provide a recirculating low-volume supply with accessible filtration and drain-down, and include an overflow to landscape drainage; verify all membranes before stone paving and planting.
projects.environmentalResponse: Place the more open court elevations toward favorable daylight and use the western perforated brick jaali, deep continuous eaves, and recessed openings to control late sun. Enable cross-ventilation through shaded rooms and the court when outdoor conditions are suitable, supplemented by fans and mechanical extraction in wet areas. Use drought-tolerant native planting, permeable paving, and captured roofwater for irrigation; keep the water feature shallow, recirculating, controllable, and optional so comfort does not depend on high water use.
